newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 3.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 3.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

MUNICH - Private television stations ProSieben and Kabel 1 increased their viewer share in the German market in May. ProSieben posted a market share of 9.1 percent in May, up from 9.0 percent in April, while Kabel 1 saw a boost to 4.0 percent, up from 3.9 percent. German market leader RTL's share dropped to 17.0 percent in May from 17.8 the previous month. Private station Sat1 also fell in the ratings, to 14.4 percent in May from 14.1 percent in April. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Saatchi & Saatchi opens a specialist health care agency in Frankfurt called Saatchi & Saatchi Healthcare Connection Germany, after having opened similar units in the U.S. and U.K. The general manager of the new shop is Wolfgang Koenig, previously account director at Sudler & Hennessey, Frankfurt. (Advertising Age)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Television company ProSieben Media AG, poised to go public on the German stock market, says it has held its market share steady in May, making the upcoming share sale even more attractive. ProSieben, which runs the ProSieben and Kabel 1 commercial television channels, says the stations' combined market share in May was unchanged at 13.1 percent.(Reuter)

BERLIN - Germany's Cartel Office begins an investigation of Deutsche Telekom over possible anti-competitive practices in its cable television operations, a spokeswoman for the office says. Private-sector broadcasters and programming producers have lodged complaints about Telekom's practices in limiting their access to its network, she says, confirming a story in Tuesday's Sueddeutsche Zeitung. (Reuter)

BERLIN - Competition among German online services is getting tougher. T-Online, Germany's biggest online service and a product of Deutsche Telekom, says it will introduce a new fee structure and billing system for its Internet offers at the end of this year. (Die Welt)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - Intel Corp is feeling pressure in Europe because of economic uncertainty in the region as well as gains by rival microchip makers, computer industry analysts. Stagnant economies, austerity measures related to European monetary union and transitions to new Intel chips are dampening demand for personal computers, especially among consumers, the analysts say. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Germany's manufacturing sector expanded at an accelerated pace in May as more bottlenecks emerged, driving up prices, according to the BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI). The index, first published last month, rose to a seasonally-adjusted 57.49 in May, the highest level yet recorded after 56.58 in April, research group NTC Publications Ltd says. (Reuter)

FUERTH - Embattled German audio-visual equipment manufacturer Grundig AG says it lost a record 631 million marks ($368.4 million) in 1996, compared with a 598 million mark loss the year before. In March, the company estimated the 1996 loss at 553 million marks. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Historically high coffee prices are no reason to abandon calls for "fairly-priced" revenue structures for smallholders and co-operatives, the press spokesman of a German campaign says. "Most Central American crops were sold ahead of the current price rallies at 140-150 cents/lb," said Harald Gruber of the German TransFair project from a Munich gathering of aligned producers and roasters."The farmer does not fully participate in the explosive gains seen in recent weeks."
(Reuter)

FREIBERG - Chemical giant Bayer AG says that it officially opened its new solar silicon production facility of Bayer Solar GmbH at Freiberg. Bayer says it has invested around 48 million marks in the facility which would give it an annual capacity of six million crystalline silicon wafers for making solar modules. (Reuter)

LEVERKUSEN/HOLZMINDEN - Bayer AG confirms a report that its Haarmann & Reimer (H&R) subsidiary was divesting its food ingredients business unit. Bayer says it is making contacts with a view to finding a buyer for the unit, which is primarily a producer of citric acid. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Lynn Bolger has become director of ad agency AP Lintas' Internet Media Department, leaving her position as head of research and planning at Softbank Interactive Marketing. AP Lintas plans to boost the department to 34 staff members by bringing in 12 new people. (Horizont)
